root.note: Taíno was spoken in the Caribbean when the Spanish arrived. Spanish patata mixes batata with papa, the Quechua word for the white potato.

history: When Spanish sailors reached the Caribbean, the Taíno people there grew batata, the sweet potato. Spanish took the word, and English made it potato in the 1500s. So the first English potatoes were sweet potatoes. The ordinary white potato came from the Andes in South America, where the Quechua word was papa. In Spain, papa and batata mixed and gave patata, and English used potato for the white one too. Other languages chose other pictures: French pomme de terre and Dutch aardappel mean ‘earth apple’, and German Kartoffel comes from an Italian word for truffle. In informal British English, a potato is a spud.
historyEinfach: Potato comes from the Caribbean. There, batata was the sweet potato. The Spanish took the word. In English it became potato. The normal white potato comes from South America. In French, a potato is an ‘earth apple’. In informal British English, it is a spud.

elsewhere.text: In Spain the potato is patata, a mix of two American words. In Latin America people say papa, the original Quechua word, and batata is still the sweet potato in many places.
German Kartoffel is not related to potato. It comes from Italian tartufolo, ‘little truffle’: both grow under the ground and look like brown lumps.
